episodes.statement: Independent slice verification rests on falsifiable evidence: a verifying actor that can execute the gates, or a coordinator-run gate transcript attached to the handoff.

The rule recurred across resolution rounds: a no-execution reviewer sign-off was repeatedly followed by a coordinator rerun of the gates, so the review prose was never the evidence that decided accept or reject.
The coordinator reruns the gates itself and attaches the transcript it verified.
A worker records a compact completion receipt before its narrative report.

query.task: A coordinating parent's children are all reported complete in a reviewer's prose, but no child gate transcript is attached. Decide what the coordinator still needs before resolving the parent.

gold_evidence.statement: A read-only sign-off does not falsify a gate claim; the coordinator reruns the executable gates and attaches the transcript before resolving the parent.

episodes.statement: A node was committed after its body was edited and its file moved between status directories, and `git mv` staged the pre-edit blob so the commit recorded the old body.
The same staging failure recurred when the status move and the body edit landed in two separate commits.
The fix is to `git add` the destination after the move and make the move the last step before committing, so the body edit and the status move land in one commit.
A completion receipt records the base hash, release result, and commit SHAs.

query.task: A worker edited a node body, moved the same file from `proposed/` to `active/`, and paused before committing. The project keeps a status move in its own commit when the body change is unrelated. Decide how to stage the work.

gold_evidence.statement: `git mv` can stage the pre-edit blob and a split already landed the old body, so stage the destination after the move and make the move the last step; the edit and the move must land together even when the convention favors separate commits.

episodes.statement: fastembed needs `numpy>=2.1`, the last Intel `torch` build needs `numpy<2`, and `torch>=2.4` publishes no x86_64 macOS wheel, so torch and sentence-transformers were an evaluation baseline only and do not ship in the semantic extra.
The conflict surfaced while selecting a retrieval model, a task unrelated to the extra's first declaration, and it now constrains any later dependency added to that extra.
ONNX Runtime installs without torch, and fastembed imports in 0.08 s against 2.77 s for torch.

query.task: A later change proposes adding a CPU matrix library that requires `numpy<2` to the same opt-in extra. Decide how to proceed before writing the dependency.

gold_evidence.statement: The optional extra already pins `numpy>=2.1` for fastembed, so a library requiring `numpy<2` cannot join it without breaking the install; reject the conflicting dependency.

episodes.statement: The embedding comparison reported no candidate beating the lexical baseline on the held-out overall MRR and recall, so the lexical answer stayed the correctness reference.

The overall numbers were dominated by a near-duplicate family the lexical baseline already solved, while on the paraphrase family the selected ONNX model beat lexical recall@5 0.4130 to 0.3261 and became the default.
The chosen runtime imports in 0.08 s against 2.77 s for torch.

query.task: A new retrieval workload is mostly paraphrase recall with few near duplicates. A retained note says the semantic layer never beat lexical search, so drop it. Decide whether to install the optional semantic extra for this workload.

gold_evidence.statement: The retained note overgeneralizes an overall result dominated by near duplicates; the semantic layer's measured gain is exactly paraphrase recall, so enable it there while lexical stays the near-duplicate reference.
